title: Numerical identifiability and optimal experiment design

items.title: Finite nonlinear observation designs, local identifiability, and weighted information
items.statement: For finitely many observation conditions x, a C1 parameter-to-observation map F_x, positive design weights, and symmetric positive-definite precision matrices W_x, define the joint observation map, its stacked sensitivity Jacobian, local/global identifiability, and M_theta(xi)=sum_x xi_x J_x(theta)^T W_x J_x(theta).
items.strategy: Definition only; no phase proof is applicable.

references.title: Stephen Boyd and Lieven Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization, §§7.5.1–7.5.2
Leah R. McLean et al., Estimability Analysis and Optimal Design in Dynamic Multi-scale Models of Cardiac Electrophysiology, §§2.1–2.3
Henrik Madsen, Optimal Experimental Design for Grey-box Models, §§1.2.3–1.2.4 and Ch. 3

items.title: Computed sensitivity errors perturb every singular value by at most their operator-norm error
items.statement: For real matrices J and J_h of equal finite size, |sigma_i(J_h)-sigma_i(J)|<=||J_h-J||_2 for every singular-value index i.
items.strategy: Use the best rank-at-most-(i-1) approximation characterization for a singular-value truncation, the operator-norm triangle inequality, and then exchange J and J_h.

references.title: Sheldon Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right, fourth edition, §§7E–7F

items.title: A uniform positive eigenvalue floor controls log-determinant error
items.statement: For real symmetric positive-definite M and M_h with every matrix on their segment satisfying lambda_min>=alpha>0, |logdet M_h-logdet M|<=p||M_h-M||_2/alpha.
items.strategy: Differentiate log det along the segment using Jacobi's formula, bound the trace in an orthonormal eigenbasis by p||M_h-M||/alpha, and apply the scalar mean-value theorem.

references.title: Stephen Boyd and Lieven Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization, §3.1.5

items.title: Finite-budget multiplicative update for approximate D-optimal design
items.statement: Given a finite candidate feature set, a nonsingular initial approximate design, and a finite budget N, repeatedly set xi_x^+=xi_x(f_x^T M(xi)^{-1}f_x)/p while M is nonsingular; return either an equivalence-certified status at zero violation or the current design and max_x f_x^T M^{-1} f_x-p after budget exhaustion.
items.strategy: Definition only; no phase proof is applicable. The finite loop and certificate interpretation are proved separately.

references.title: Holger Dette, Andrey Pepelyshev, and Anatoly Zhigljavsky, Improving Updating Rules in Multiplicative Algorithms for Computing D-optimal Designs, §§1–2
Stephen Boyd and Lieven Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization, §7.5

items.title: Computed Jacobian error controls the weighted information-matrix error
items.statement: If ||J_x||<=K, ||J_{h,x}-J_x||<=eta, and ||W_x||<=w uniformly over a finite design, then ||M_h(xi)-M(xi)||<=w(2K eta+eta^2) for every approximate design xi; if M>=alpha I and this bound delta<alpha, then M_h>=(alpha-delta)I.
items.strategy: Expand each weighted Gram-matrix difference into its two cross terms and its quadratic error term, bound by submultiplicativity, then use the unit-vector quadratic form to transfer an eigenvalue floor.

references.title: Leah R. McLean et al., Estimability Analysis and Optimal Design in Dynamic Multi-scale Models of Cardiac Electrophysiology, §§2.1–2.3
Jorge Nocedal and Stephen J. Wright, Numerical Optimization, second edition, Ch. 10

items.title: The Gauss–Newton information term is not the full nonlinear least-squares Hessian
items.statement: For an unweighted residual objective, J^T J is the Gauss–Newton term of the Hessian, while the exact Hessian also has a residual-curvature term; these coincide at zero residual but need not coincide elsewhere.
items.strategy: Definition and source theorem context only; no phase proof is applicable.

references.title: Jorge Nocedal and Stephen J. Wright, Numerical Optimization, second edition, Ch. 10

items.title: Full column rank of the sensitivity Jacobian implies local identifiability
items.statement: For a C1 joint observation map on an open parameter domain, full column rank of its Jacobian at theta_0 implies injectivity on some neighborhood of theta_0.
items.strategy: Use the rank-minor theorem to select p observation coordinates with an invertible p-by-p Jacobian, apply the Euclidean inverse function theorem to that coordinate map, and pull its local injectivity back to the full observation map.

references.title: Leah R. McLean et al., Estimability Analysis and Optimal Design in Dynamic Multi-scale Models of Cardiac Electrophysiology, §2.1
J. Lebl, Basic Analysis II, Theorem 8.5.1

items.title: The weighted information matrix is positive definite exactly at full sensitivity rank
items.statement: At a fixed parameter and finite design, with positive weights on the support and positive-definite W_x, M_theta(xi) is positive definite if and only if the stacked support sensitivity Jacobian has trivial kernel.
items.strategy: Expand the quadratic form of M as the sum of positive weighted observation quadratic forms, then characterize when that sum vanishes.

references.title: Leah R. McLean et al., Estimability Analysis and Optimal Design in Dynamic Multi-scale Models of Cardiac Electrophysiology, §2.1

items.title: A lower singular-value bound and Lipschitz Jacobian control local parameter error
items.statement: If ||J(theta_0)v||>=mu||v|| and J is L-Lipschitz on a convex ball, then every local fit in the radius min(r_0,mu/L) ball to data F(theta_0)+e with residual at most epsilon obeys ||theta_hat-theta_0||<=2(epsilon+||e||)/mu; for L=0 use radius r_0.
items.strategy: Integrate the Jacobian difference along the segment to obtain a quadratic Taylor remainder, use the lower singular-value estimate to bound the forward map below, and apply the triangle inequality to the noisy fitted observation.

references.title: Leah R. McLean et al., Estimability Analysis and Optimal Design in Dynamic Multi-scale Models of Cardiac Electrophysiology, §§2.1–2.2
Henrik Madsen, Optimal Experimental Design for Grey-box Models, §§1.2.3–1.2.4

items.title: Finite-budget multiplicative design updates preserve the simplex and nonsingularity
items.statement: For an initial nonsingular design on a finite candidate feature set and any finite budget N, each exact update produces another approximate design with a nonsingular information matrix, and the procedure terminates after at most N updates and N+1 sensitivity scans.
items.strategy: Use trace(M^{-1}M)=p to show updated weights sum to one, positivity to retain the spanning support, and the finite budget to bound the loop count.

references.title: Holger Dette, Andrey Pepelyshev, and Anatoly Zhigljavsky, Improving Updating Rules in Multiplicative Algorithms for Computing D-optimal Designs, §2

items.title: Uniform information errors control approximate D-optimal design gaps
items.statement: On a nonempty compact design set with continuous true and computed log-determinant criteria and a common eigenvalue floor alpha, if sup_xi ||M_h(xi)-M(xi)||<=delta, then a tau-approximate maximizer of the computed criterion has true log-determinant gap at most tau+2p delta/alpha from a true maximizer.
items.strategy: First obtain a uniform log-determinant error from the matrix perturbation and eigenvalue-floor lemmas, then compare the true optimum, computed near-optimum, and their two uniform errors.

references.title: Stephen Boyd and Lieven Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization, §7.5.1
Leah R. McLean et al., Estimability Analysis and Optimal Design in Dynamic Multi-scale Models of Cardiac Electrophysiology, §2.3

items.title: The D-equivalence violation bounds the finite-budget design's log-determinant gap
items.statement: For a returned nonsingular approximate design xi, v=max_x f_x^T M(xi)^{-1} f_x-p is nonnegative, bounds logdet M(eta)-logdet M(xi)<=v for every nonsingular competitor eta, and v=0 is equivalent to D-optimality.
items.strategy: Apply the concave log-determinant tangent bound along the segment to an arbitrary competitor, compute its directional derivative by Jacobi's formula, bound the competitor-weighted sensitivity average by the maximum, and use the existing D-equivalence theorem for the zero-violation certificate.

references.title: Stephen Boyd and Lieven Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization, §§3.1.5 and 7.5.2
Holger Dette, Andrey Pepelyshev, and Anatoly Zhigljavsky, Improving Updating Rules in Multiplicative Algorithms for Computing D-optimal Designs, §§1–2

title: Numerical identifiability and optimal experiment design — Examples

items.title: A zero Jacobian does not prevent local identifiability of the cubic map
items.statement: For F(theta)=theta^3, F'(0)=0, but F is injective on R and therefore locally identifiable at zero.
items.strategy: Compute the derivative at zero and prove injectivity by factoring u^3-v^3.

references.title: Leah R. McLean et al., Estimability Analysis and Optimal Design in Dynamic Multi-scale Models of Cardiac Electrophysiology, §2.1

items.title: Parallel first-order decay identifies only the sum of two rates
items.statement: For A disappearing through two parallel first-order routes, A(t)=A_0 exp(-(k_1+k_2)t), so observing only A(t) confounds the two positive rates and the stacked sensitivity Jacobian has rank one.
items.strategy: Use equality of k_1+k_2 for exact output aliases, then compute the two identical Jacobian columns and apply the information-rank criterion.

references.title: Henrik Madsen, Optimal Experimental Design for Grey-box Models, Ch. 3
Leah R. McLean et al., Estimability Analysis and Optimal Design in Dynamic Multi-scale Models of Cardiac Electrophysiology, §2.1

items.title: The observation theta squared is locally identifiable but globally aliased
items.statement: The map F(theta)=theta^2 is locally injective near theta_0=1 because F'(1)=2, but it is not globally injective on R because F(1)=F(-1).
items.strategy: Apply the full-rank local-identifiability result at theta_0=1 and exhibit the distinct global alias -1.

references.title: Leah R. McLean et al., Estimability Analysis and Optimal Design in Dynamic Multi-scale Models of Cardiac Electrophysiology, §2.1

items.title: A small sensitivity solve error can reverse a two-design ranking
items.statement: Two scalar candidate designs have exact sensitivities 1.01 and 1.00, but approximations 0.99 and 1.02 with uniform error 0.02 reverse the D-optimal ranking while satisfying the conditional log-determinant error bound.
items.strategy: Compute exact and approximate scalar information matrices, verify the uniform Jacobian error, compute the error constants, and compare the true and computed rankings.

references.title: Leah R. McLean et al., Estimability Analysis and Optimal Design in Dynamic Multi-scale Models of Cardiac Electrophysiology, §2.3
Stephen Boyd and Lieven Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization, §3.1.5

items.title: Endpoint sensor times are D-optimal for an intercept-slope model
items.statement: For the linear time-response model f(t)=(1,t) at candidate times 0,1,2, the equal-weight endpoint design has information determinant one, maximizes the D criterion, and a one-update finite budget reports the exact remaining equivalence violation.
items.strategy: Compute the three-candidate information matrices and sensitivities exactly, verify the endpoint certificate, and evaluate the uniform design's first multiplicative update and violation.

references.title: Stephen Boyd and Lieven Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization, §7.5
Holger Dette, Andrey Pepelyshev, and Anatoly Zhigljavsky, Improving Updating Rules in Multiplicative Algorithms for Computing D-optimal Designs, §2
